clue.text: Old lady is proverbially safe in her city street

definitions.text: Old lady is proverbially safe in her city street

parts.words: Old lady is proverbially safe in her city street
parts.note: the Old Lady of Threadneedle Street is the nickname of Britain's central bank, in the City of London, and 'as safe as' it is a proverb

explanation.walkthrough: Threadneedle Street is in the City, London's financial district; the bank there has long been called 'the Old Lady', and anything secure is 'as safe as' that bank.
explanation.definitionFit: The national bank of the United Kingdom is nicknamed the Old Lady of Threadneedle Street and is the byword for safety.

clue.text: Living for food ?

definitions.meaning: a livelihood, the basic means of earning one's keep
plain everyday fare, slices spread with a dairy fat

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means one's basic livelihood and also, literally, a staple snack of sliced loaf spread with dairy fat.

clue.text: Directions to friend to land north of India

parts.note: N is the compass abbreviation for north
E is the compass abbreviation for east
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone gives a friend directions to a country beyond India's northern border.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan kingdom lies along India's northern frontier.

clue.text: Speaker swallows one gin as a starter

indicators.note: a speaker who swallows something takes it inside, so these letters go within the word for speaker

parts.note: an orator is a speaker
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A public speaker downs a gin before beginning his address.
explanation.definitionFit: One who originates something is the person who starts it off.

clue.text: Developed specifically as per theory

parts.note: developed in the particular manner Darwin's theory describes, by natural selection over generations

explanation.definitionFit: Species changed over time by natural selection, as Darwin's theory has it, are said to have done so.

clue.text: Tragic confusion about old Bob-attributed to stomach

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, that is around, the next piece
confusion of the word tragic means its letters are jumbled

parts.note: a bob was the old British shilling, abbreviated s

explanation.surface: A muddled tragedy about an old coin is blamed on someone's belly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusion' turns TRAGIC into GATRIC, and 'about' puts S inside it. A bob was a shilling in Britain's pre-1971 money, written s.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to or located in the belly.

clue.text: It could be the end of the church

definitions.text: It could be the end of the church

parts.words: It could be the end of the church
parts.note: the end here is the physical eastern end of a church building, not its demise

explanation.definitionFit: This vaulted recess usually forms the rounded eastern end of a church building.

clue.text: What Holmes made gets taken away

definitions.meaning: Sherlock Holmes reasoned from clues to conclusions
an amount subtracted, as from pay

explanation.definitionFit: The detective's logical inferences and a subtraction from a sum share this one noun.

clue.text: Ruling on precedence for members of an administrative body ?

definitions.text: Ruling on precedence for members of an administrative body ?

parts.words: Ruling on precedence for members of an administrative body
parts.note: read literally, a decision about who ranks first among the members of a governing board

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain this is a government decree issued by the monarch on the advice of the Privy Council; the clue reads it as a ruling on the ranking order within a council.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree made by the sovereign through the Privy Council, here read as sorting the rank of councillors.

clue.text: Makes deadly involved spoonerism, right away

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are rearranged
right away means the letter for right is removed

explanation.surface: A slip of the tongue gets so tangled it becomes fatal, at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' takes R out of SPOONERISM, leaving SPOONEISM, which 'involved' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To poison something is to make it lethal.

clue.text: Man's predecessor in a bishopric

parts.note: the Anglican diocese on the Isle of Man is styled with a two-part name, and Man is the second part

explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man's diocese is 'Sodor and Man', so in the title one word comes before 'Man'; the surface suggests an earlier bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: The diocese title 'Sodor and Man' puts this name first, before the island's.

clue.text: Idle hour wandering in new Indian city

indicators.note: wandering letters drift from their places, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An idle hour spent roaming around a newly built Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' rearranges IDLE plus H. 'in new' is a link: the answer sits in 'New ___', the Indian capital New Delhi.
explanation.definitionFit: The city in northern India, containing the capital New Delhi.

clue.text: A girl to rave about

indicators.note: about here means around and around, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A girl gets everybody to enthuse about her.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female first name.

clue.text: A cheerful view here of pain

indicators.note: the answer is to be seen here, within the words in front of it

explanation.surface: A bright outlook is to be found here despite suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull continuous hurt is a kind of pain.

clue.text: It may show illustrations to foster class-consciousness

definitions.text: It may show illustrations to foster class-consciousness

parts.words: It may show illustrations to foster class-consciousness
parts.note: class means a school class, and consciousness its awareness of a lesson drawn up at the front of the room

explanation.definitionFit: A teacher chalks diagrams on this dark board at the front of a schoolroom so pupils pay attention.

clue.text: Worker gets little sleep to start with — that's a safe bet

indicators.note: the little sleep comes at the start, before the worker

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep
a hand is a manual worker

explanation.surface: A labourer snatches a short doze first, sure that's a safe thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: In the card game nap, winning all five tricks is a nap hand, so the phrase means a position certain to pay off.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding a hand that is sure to win every trick makes a near-certain wager.

clue.text: Judging by results, it could be part magic

indicators.note: it could be signals that the words might become something else when their letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone judging solely by outcomes suspects partial sorcery.
explanation.definitionFit: A practical approach judges things by their consequences rather than theory.

clue.text: He's welcome to a cell in Italian capital

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: a capital letter is the first one, so take the first letter of Italian

explanation.surface: A man is welcomed into a prison cell in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: The Italian goldsmith Benvenuto Cellini: his first name means 'welcome', which makes 'He's welcome' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Benvenuto, the Renaissance goldsmith's first name, is Italian for welcome.

clue.text: Confirm alarm call from zoo??

definitions.meaning: to support or corroborate a claim
a warning shout that a big furry beast has escaped its enclosure

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means corroborate, and read literally it warns that a grizzly is loose.

clue.text: No strife with my old Dutch? Bother the rest!

definitions.text: No strife with my old Dutch? Bother the rest!

parts.words: No strife with my old Dutch? Bother the rest!
parts.note: without the strife, the rest of the phrase is left, which also means bother

explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang: 'trouble and strife' = wife, and 'my old Dutch' (from 'Duchess of Fife') also means wife. Drop 'strife' and the rest of the slang phrase remains, a word meaning bother.
explanation.definitionFit: Bother and difficulty are synonyms, and the word is what remains of the slang for wife.

clue.text: The French section is sparing of words

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the
a conic is a conic section, a curve cut from a cone

explanation.surface: A passage in French is notably brief.
explanation.definitionFit: A terse speaker uses very few words.

clue.text: Liaison officer carrying the torch

definitions.meaning: a person who connects others, such as a broadcaster joining segments
a link was a torch, and a man employed to carry one lit people through dark streets

explanation.definitionFit: A presenter joining items is one sense; a link-boy, who bore a flaming brand through streets, is the old other.

clue.text: May be on the cob-less pleasant if on foot

definitions.meaning: maize grain is eaten on its cob
a painful hard patch of skin on a toe

explanation.definitionFit: Maize on its cob and a hard painful lump on a toe share one word.

clue.text: African .graduate with hard nut to crack

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate

indicators.note: cracking a nut breaks it apart, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An African graduate has a difficult problem to solve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with hard' is surface padding from the phrase 'a hard nut to crack'; 'to crack' rearranges NUT to NTU.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bantu are a large family of peoples of central and southern Africa.

clue.text: A chemical-the first one, we hear, for a playgoer

indicators.note: we hear means the word is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a first-nighter is a theatregoer at an opening performance, so the first one ... for a playgoer suggests this word

explanation.surface: A chemical, so rumour says, was the first of its kind for theatre fans.
explanation.walkthrough: A playgoer at a premiere is a first-nighter; the word after 'first' is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Potassium nitrate, saltpetre, is a chemical compound.

clue.text: Girl to' hold "love-in soon

indicators.note: the girl is to hold, that is contain, the next piece

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A girl is due to host a love-in shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old word for shortly or presently.

clue.text: Suffering consumption at school, say'

indicators.note: say signals a word spoken aloud that matches the answer

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A pupil at boarding school is ill with tuberculosis.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is an elite English boarding school near Windsor; 'consumption' looks like the old disease but means being consumed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something devoured has undergone being consumed.

clue.text: New style combs, a-bit highfalutin

indicators.note: a new style rearranges the words into a fresh form, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A fresh way of combing one's hair is a little pretentious.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompous, inflated language is pretentious.

clue.text: Accommodation passed unfit for a hermit (if not for a criminal)

definitions.text: Accommodation passed unfit for a hermit (if not for a criminal)

parts.words: Accommodation passed unfit for a hermit (if not for a criminal)
parts.note: a hermit's cell declared uninhabitable; for a criminal the same phrase means where a prisoner awaits execution

explanation.definitionFit: A prison room for someone sentenced to death, read also as a monk's room ruled unfit to live in.
